bird-removal.intro: Bird work in Pomaria is vent-and-chimney work in deep farm country. This small Newberry County community of farmhouses, barns, and older rural homes sits in the rolling country along the old Columbia highway, and its bird problems follow the structures: starlings and sparrows in the bathroom and kitchen vent runs of the farmhouses, chimney swifts in the uncapped brick flues each summer, pigeons in the barn lofts and under the equipment sheds, and woodpeckers working the siding of the quieter houses. Most bird calls here are noise and mess complaints — a vent full of nesting material is also a fire and moisture problem, which is why the fix is mechanical, not chemical: the birds out, the opening covered, the flue capped.
bird-removal.extendedBody:
Vents, flues, and the legal line

Pomaria's vent birds are mostly starlings and house sparrows — unprotected species that can be removed and excluded directly, and the work is the cover: vent runs cleaned of nesting material and fitted with proper covers that still let the fan breathe, because a blocked bathroom vent trades a bird problem for a mould problem. Chimney swifts are the exception that matters: they are federally protected, they nest in uncapped chimneys from May into the fall, and they cannot legally be disturbed while nesting — the honest answer for a swift chimney is to enjoy the summer tenants and cap the flue after they leave for South America, which we schedule and do. Woodpecker damage on the farmhouses is read before it is answered: drumming in spring is usually territorial and seasonal, while excavation means insects in the siding or a cavity being built, and the two problems have different solutions. Farm buildings get the practical version — pigeon roosting in a barn is ended with netting and perch denial at the roost beams, not with poisons anywhere near feed.

faqs.q: Birds are nesting in our Pomaria bathroom vent and it smells. What is involved?
faqs.a: The nest and its material come out — that debris is the smell, and it is also a genuine fire and moisture hazard in a vent run — and the exterior opening is fitted with a proper bird-proof cover that preserves the fan's airflow. If the vent birds are starlings or sparrows, as they almost always are here, removal is straightforward and legal at any season. We check the full run while we are there, because a vent that has hosted one nest has usually been used before, and the attic end of the story is worth knowing about before we close the outside end.

faqs.q: Chimney swifts are in our Pomaria flue and we hear them all summer. Can they be removed?
faqs.a: Not while they are nesting — chimney swifts are protected by federal law, and disturbing an active swift nest is illegal for us and for you. The good news is the tenancy is temporary and, by most accounts, charming: they eat insects all summer and leave for South America in the fall. The permanent fix is scheduled, not immediate: once they have gone, we cap the flue with a proper chimney cap, and the swifts return the next spring to find the address closed and move to a tree or a neighbour's uncapped flue. We will book the capping for the fall window when we inspect.

squirrel-removal.intro: Newberry's squirrels work a college town's canopy. The county seat's historic district and the Newberry College neighbourhoods stand under some of the upstate's finest street trees — mature oaks over early-1900s homes with tall, layered rooflines — and gray squirrels move through that canopy roof to roof, chewing in at the soffits and gable vents of the older housing and denning in its attics through the winter. The surrounding county is farm and timber, the town's creeks run to the Saluda, and the squirrel population an old Newberry roof contends with is stocked from every direction. The entries here are the historic-district standard: wherever a porch roof or an addition met the original house across the last century.
squirrel-removal.extendedBody:
Historic rooflines under a college-town canopy

Newberry exclusions are won in the mapping. A century-old roofline offers a colony multiple entries, and sealing the active one promotes the next — so we read the whole perimeter: every junction, gable, and flashing line, plus the canopy bridges that deliver the squirrels to them. The colony is excluded with one-way devices, the entries rebuilt in metal fitted to sit quietly on old trim, and the limbs bridging to the roof mapped for your tree crew. Student rentals and quiet owner homes alike get the photographic record, because Newberry has plenty of owners who manage from a distance and a report they cannot verify is a bill they cannot trust. The attic read covers nesting, droppings, and wiring — in the historic district especially, a colony of several seasons is a wiring conversation, and we have it with photographs and plain language.

faqs.q: How much does squirrel removal cost in Newberry?
faqs.a: It depends on the roofline — a newer home with one chewed soffit is a compact job; a historic-district house with junctions from three additions is a mapping exercise and a bigger seal. We inspect the whole perimeter and the canopy over it, then quote firmly before work starts, with the photographic record included. The sealing materials are specified to sit quietly on old trim, because in the historic district how the work looks is part of the work.

faqs.q: Squirrels get into our Newberry rental property every year. Can it be ended for good?
faqs.a: Yes — annual recurrence means annual use of the same entries, because squirrels return to proven dens and the patched-in-kind repairs of past seasons are being re-chewed on schedule. The end of the cycle is a complete seal in metal at every entry, not just the active one, plus the canopy bridges cut. Rentals benefit most: the work is done once, documented photographically for the owner, and the property stops generating the autumn call. Bring us the history when we inspect — which years, which rooms heard noise — because it usually maps the entries better than the squirrels do.

opossum-removal.intro: Newberry's opossums work the seam between the college town and the country around it. Virginia opossums den under the porches and in the crawlspaces of the historic district's older homes, in the carriage houses and outbuildings behind them, and under the quieter student rentals — commuting at night along the fence lines and creek branches toward the Saluda. The town's older housing offers them a den map of unusual richness, and the spring pattern is reliable: females denning under houses with litters, dogs announcing them at the vents, and homeowners discovering that the tenant under the porch has been there since February. They are gentle, useful, and entirely evictable — provided the den closes behind them.
opossum-removal.extendedBody:
Historic dens and the rental problem

Newberry opossum work is screening work on old buildings. The resident is trapped or excluded — timed around any litter, because a spring exclusion that separates a mother from her young is a failure with a smell attached — and then the voids close: porch perimeters in buried mesh, crawlspace vents replaced, the gaps under the district's additions and carriage houses sealed. Rentals get the documented version: landlords here manage from a distance, and the photographic record of the den, the eviction, and the screen is the deliverable that ends the annual call. Removal runs under the depredation permit for the property. Around the college streets the food conversation is half the cure — bins that seal, no pet food on porches — because an opossum's map of Newberry is a map of its dinners, and the dens cluster where the dinners are reliable.

faqs.q: How much does opossum removal cost in Newberry?
faqs.a: It depends on the building — a single porch den is compact; a historic home with crawlspace, porch, and carriage-house voids is a screening programme. We inspect, quote removal and closing as one firm price, and include the photographic record, which rental owners in particular will want for their files. Spring jobs are timed around any litter in residence, and that timing is part of the quote, stated plainly at the inspection.

faqs.q: Our Newberry tenants report an opossum under the rental's porch with babies. What is the process?
faqs.a: The family is handled on its own calendar. A mother opossum with young in the pouch or denning is either trapped as a family once the young are mobile, or given the short window until they are, with the exclusion and screening scheduled immediately after — the one thing we will not do is seal a den with young inside it. You get the plan and the dates in writing, with photographs at each stage, so the tenants and your records both know exactly what is happening and when the porch becomes the tenants' again.
